_readme: One reward track per character: the hundred-level rail on the reward-track screen, levels 2-100 (RewardTrack.StartingLevel/MaxLevel; level 1 is where a character starts, not somewhere they arrive). A track is described, not levelled -- an author writes twelve milestones and a filler mix, and the game computes where every filler node lands. EVERY TRACK SHARES THE SAME TWELVE MILESTONE LEVELS -- 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 45, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100 -- because the screen bakes milestone-ness (disc size, ring sprite, caption font) into the built scene at build time; only the CONTENT at each level is per-character. The remaining 87 levels are FILLER, authored as a MIX of (reward, amount, count) rows rather than as levels: 'count' is how many of the 87 filler levels that row occupies, and 'amount' is what it pays each time. A character with no entry in 'tracks' gets RewardTrackDefinition.Default instead -- the spine (Respec at 20, ten stat points at 80, a second life at 90) plus MaxHealth at the other nine milestones and a StatPoint/MaxHealth filler mix, so an undesigned character still shows a plain, honest track rather than a blank or broken one. The five validation rules RewardTrackEntryResolver enforces: (1) every one of the twelve milestone levels carries exactly one entry, and no entry names a level that is not one of the twelve; (2) the filler counts in one track's 'filler' array sum to exactly 87; (3) a one-shot capability -- Respec, SecondLife, SignatureAbsorbs, UnlockSkill -- may only be a milestone, never filler, because filler's placement is computed and always starts at level 2, before an author could deliberately delay it; (4) a FILLER ElementalDamagePercent entry's 'against' must be an element the character can already deal at level 1 (their own attackType, or a damageInstances type on a skill authored to them with unlockLevel <= 1) -- a milestone is exempt, since its level is authored and visible, so a milestone element can be placed deliberately after the skill that first deals it; (5) a signature reward (SignatureCapacity/GainPerTurn/GainOnDamageTaken/Absorbs) is refused on a character with no signatureId, because BuildSignatureResource would have nothing to pay it into. WHERE A FILLER NODE LANDS: the mix's declaration order does not matter, but the counts do -- InterleaveMix picks, at each of the 87 free levels in order starting from level 2, whichever row is furthest behind the share its count entitles it to (ties go to declaration order), so the row with the biggest count always takes level 2 and every row repeats at roughly its own even cadence across the whole track. reward is a TrackReward enum member name, matched case-insensitively; against is a DamageType name (Ice, not the skill-JSON-only alias Frost), read only by ElementalDamagePercent; skillId is read only by UnlockSkill and must name a real skill id -- the track's skill branch carries no ownership test, so a track may grant a skill authored to a different character (docs/PLAN_REWARD_TRACKS.md §3f/§3h). Field-by-field documentation, defaults and valid enum values: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md. Design rationale for these two tracks: docs/PLAN_REWARD_TRACKS.md §5.
